question.worked_solution:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}(\theta )\text{d}\theta \,.
$$

When $r(\theta )=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $, ${\theta }_{1}=0$ and ${\theta }_{2}=\frac{\pi }{2}$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =8{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =8\cdot \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =4\theta \,{|}_{0}^{\pi /2}+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =4(\frac{\pi }{2}-0)+2(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡0) \\  & =2\pi +0 \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
